text:
emma: Customer reported weird negative tokens/sec and TTFT spikes after their weekend deploy. Dashboard shows -32 tokens/sec for a handful of hosts :grimacing:

raj: Ugh. Any correlating errors in the logs? Kafka restarts? Consumer group rebalance?

emma: They said they saw a Kafka broker bounce at 02:13 UTC. I pulled the streaming dashboard and the negative values start exactly after that.

liam: Negative rates usually mean counter reset or wrong PromQL. Are we using rate()/increase() on a counter that got rolled back?

marta: Paging infra team to confirm if we had any consumer restarts around that time. infra-bot: incident created #INC-2026-443 - investigating.

raj: Can someone run these quick checks: 1) curl /metrics for streamer on affected host 2) check kafka-consumer-groups --describe for group offsets 3) query prom: sum(rate(redwood_streaming_tokens_total[1m])) by (instance)

emma: Ran curl on host stream-03: ```
$ curl -s http://stream-03.internal:9100/metrics | grep redwood_streaming_tokens_total
redwood_streaming_tokens_total{instance="stream-03",job="streamer"} 0
```
But prometheus shows past samples with small positive then a jump to a smaller number -> rate() computed negative.

liam: That matches counter reset scenario. Kafka bounce probably restarted the streamer process and its counter restarted at 0; Prometheus rate() sees drop and computes negative slope for that scrape interval. Shouldn't rate() produce a negative? Usually it guards, but if metric name changed or exporter returned older timestamps it can.

emma: kafka-consumer-groups output from that timeframe: ```
$ kafka-consumer-groups.sh --bootstrap-server brokers:9092 --group streamer-v1 --describe
GROUP           TOPIC           PARTITION  CURRENT-OFFSET  LOG-END-OFFSET  LAG  CONSUMER-ID
streamer-v1     stream-events    0          123450          123460          10   consumer-7 (stream-03)
```
No obvious extreme jump.

marta: I checked k8s events — stream-03 restarted pod 02:13:27 due to OOM. Logs show process exit and immediate restart. Prometheus scrape interval is 15s.

raj: Ok. Two contributing issues: exporter counter reset on restart + our dashboard uses delta of raw gauge derived from the counter which yields transient negative points. We should use increase() in the panels and ignore negative deltas. Also add a Prometheus recording rule to drop negative deltas.

liam: For immediate mitigation: 1) add a dashboard panel transformation to clamp values to >=0 2) backfill the affected timeslices in the analytics pipeline using the request logs to compute tokens/sec if accurate historical is required.

emma: Customer wants a clear RCA and repro steps. Proposed repro: 1) start streamer locally, increment redwood_streaming_tokens_total to ~1000, 2) restart process so counter resets to 0, 3) wait for two scrapes, 4) run prom query `rate(redwood_streaming_tokens_total[1m])` and observe negative/near-zero around restart.

raj: Can also reproduce by pushing a lower timestamped metric sample (bad exporter) — that will create negative rate in some Grafana functions. But OOM/restart is more realistic.

marta: Action items: @raj patch dashboards + add recording rule, @liam produce short script to backfill tokens/sec in analytics, @emma prepare customer-facing message explaining cause and workaround.

infra-bot: deploy job queued: job/patch-dashboard-2026 started by raj.

liam: Backfill plan: run a one-off job that replays request logs and emits derived tokens/sec metrics into the metrics-backfill topic, then our analytics job can re-ingest for the window 02:10-02:20 UTC. I can prepare the job today.

emma: Draft customer note: "We investigated and found the negative TTFT and tokens/sec were caused by streamer processes restarting after a Kafka broker bounce. When the internal token counters reset, our dashboard panel computed transient negative rates. We have a dashboard fix (clamp/recording rule) and a backfill plan to repair the analytics window. No user data was lost." Thoughts?

raj: Sounds good. Add ETA for fix and backfill. Also include that long-term we should make counters use monotonic metrics with process uptime labels and let Prometheus handle resets with increase() wrappers.

marta: Also check billing pipeline — billing uses token counts aggregated by analytics job. If we have negative deltas feeding billing, we should ensure billing ingestion discards negatives. Can someone confirm billing pipeline behavior?

emma: Reached out to billing, they confirmed the ingestion layer currently sums raw delta values and would double-check. I've flagged as potential billing risk and asked for rollback/compensation policy if any negative deltas made it into invoices.

raj: Good catch. For immediate guardrails we should: 1) reject negative delta samples in analytics ingest 2) add alerts for any negative tokens/sec across more than 2 consecutive scrapes 3) fix Grafana panels.

emma: I'll send the customer an update in 30m with current mitigation and ETA for backfill. Marking thread for follow-ups. :white_check_mark:
